dhp60:2: Long is the night for one awake, long is a league for one tired,
dhp60:4: long is the round of births and deaths for fools who know not True Dhamma.
dhp61:1: If while roaming one cannot find one better or the same as oneself,
dhp61:3: one should resolve to go alone: there is no friendship with fools.
dhp62:1: “Sons are mine, riches are mine,” so the fool suffers vexation,
dhp62:3: when even self is not his own, how then sons, how then riches?
dhp63:1: The fool who knows (his) foolishness, is at least wise in that (matter),
dhp63:3: the fool who is proud of his wisdom, he is said to be a fool indeed.
dhp64:2: Even if a fool attends on a wise man for his whole life long,
dhp64:3: he does not learn Dhamma, just as spoon learns not the taste of curry.
dhp65:2: If a perceptive man attends on a wise man even for a second,
dhp65:3: he quickly learns Dhamma, just as the tongue (learns) the taste of curry.
dhp66:1: Stupid fools live having themselves as their own foes,
dhp66:3: committing wicked deeds, which produce bitter fruit.
dhp67:1: That deed is not well done, which, having done, one has regret,
dhp67:3: for which he has tears on his face, as the result follows him round.
dhp68:1: But that deed is well done, which, having done, one has no regret,
dhp68:3: for which he is pleased and happy, as the result follows him round.
dhp69:2: The fool thinks it sweet, as long as the wicked deed does not ripen,
dhp69:3: but when the wicked deed ripens, the fool undergoes suffering.
dhp70:1: From month to month the fool may eat food with the tip of kusa-grass,
dhp70:3: (but) he is not worth a sixteenth part of those who have mastered Dhamma.
dhp71:2: A wicked deed that has been done, like milk, does not turn all at once,
dhp71:4: smouldering, it follows the fool, like a fire covered with ashes.
dhp72:2: As far as learning arises for a fool, it is only to his disadvantage,
dhp72:3: it destroys the fool’s good fortune, and it will destroy his head.
dhp73:2: He may wish for the respect that is lacking, and status amongst the monastics,
dhp73:3: for control in the living quarters, and worship amongst good families:
dhp74:1: “Householders and renunciants should both think this was done by me,
dhp74:4: let them (all) be under my sway, in all to be done and not done”,
dhp74:6: so does the fool think, (meanwhile) his desires and conceit increase.
dhp75:1: For the means to gains is one thing, the (path) going to Nibbāna another,
dhp75:4: thus knowing this the monastic disciple of the Buddha
dhp75:5: should not delight in honours, (but) practise in solitude.
dhp75:7: The Chapter about Fools, the Fifth
